notes: ORIGIN BUILD HOST = WINDOWS. rustc bakes dep paths into panic strings; on Windows they are backslash Windows paths (C:\Users\<user>\.cargo\git\checkouts\...). The verifier reproduces in a Linux container, where rustc cannot emit those bytes - no HOME/remap setting reconstructs them. This artifact is therefore NOT sandbox-reproducible by design of the host, not by any missing pin.

TOOL GAP 1: buildinfo::wasm::reverse PATH_MARKERS are POSIX-only (/home/, /Users/, /root/, .cargo/registry/src/). A Windows build matches none, so reverse reports home=None/host_triple=None and - because the rustc-internal /rustc/<hash>/ paths ARE present - sets remapped=true, i.e. it reads a Windows build as an already-remapped one. Suggested: also scan for [A-Z]:\ and surface the host OS.
TOOL GAP 2: c_toolchain.source.method has no wasi-sdk variant (apt|llvm-release|homebrew-bottle), though wasi-sdk is what both predicate deploys used for the C leg.

The Linux build IS byte-deterministic: two clean rebuilds under the same HOME gave the identical sha256 1d2c9f1c...; only changing HOME moves it (46e6263a... under a different HOME). So a Linux-built deployment of this crate WOULD verify byte-exact once environment.home is pinned.
